target.title: fix: sSH transport security check rejects connection before tunnel is established
target.body:
## Summary

- Fixes configured remote Gateway SSH transport so config-derived `ws://` remote URLs are classified as managed SSH targets before the plaintext guard rejects them.
- Starts the managed SSH tunnel for the owning Gateway client paths, rewrites the runtime URL to loopback, and closes the tunnel on one-shot call completion or long-lived client shutdown/startup failure.
- Keeps the security boundary narrow: CLI/env URL overrides, explicit `transport: "direct"`, and SSH configs without `sshTarget` still use the existing plaintext `ws://` safety path.
- Keeps omitted `gateway.remote.transport` on the documented SSH default when an SSH target is configured, and keeps omitted `gateway.remote.remotePort` on the remote-side Gateway default port `18789`.

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fixes #26250, where configured SSH transport could be rejected by the remote plaintext `ws://` security check before the SSH tunnel was established.
- Ensures configured SSH remote Gateway calls/bootstrap clients establish the managed tunnel first and connect through the local forwarded endpoint.
- Ensures ACP, MCP channel bridge, and operator approval clients release the bootstrap tunnel when they stop or fail during startup.

Why does this matter now?

Issue #26250 blocks the documented safe remote Gateway setup: the configured URL is intentionally a remote endpoint that should become a local SSH-forwarded endpoint before the Gateway client opens a websocket.

What is the intended outcome?

Configured SSH remote users can keep `gateway.remote.url` as the Gateway endpoint and `gateway.remote.sshTarget` as the SSH host. OpenClaw starts the tunnel, rewrites the runtime connection to `127.0.0.1:<localPort>`, uses `gateway.remote.remotePort` or the default remote Gateway port, and cleans up the tunnel when the owning path finishes or fails.

What is intentionally out of scope?

This does not change CLI/env Gateway URL override safety, make `transport: "direct"` bypass plaintext protection, add WSS-over-SSH SNI behavior, add reconnect tunnel restart behavior, change status/health/doctor/TUI/security-audit/logs/devices/Crestodian behavior, add a schema migration, or introduce a new transport protocol.

What does success look like?

A config-derived SSH remote can use a non-loopback `ws://` configured URL without being rejected before tunnel startup; the actual runtime websocket target is loopback; explicit direct/override paths still reject unsafe plaintext remotes; and owned SSH tunnels do not leak after call/client shutdown or startup failure.

What should reviewers focus on?

Please focus on the managed SSH ownership boundary: only config-derived remote URLs with SSH transport ownership and `sshTarget` receive the pre-tunnel plaintext allowance, and the runtime URL is rewritten to loopback immediately after tunnel startup.

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for configured SSH remote Gateway transport validation and lifecycle ownership.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the owned Gateway call/bootstrap scope covered by this PR; the remaining probe-path bot finding is disclosed below as out of scope because status/health/doctor probe surfaces are intentionally unchanged.
- Root cause: The source validation contract checked the raw config-derived remote Gateway URL before the configured SSH transport owner created the tunnel and transformed that URL into the loopback runtime endpoint. A configured SSH remote therefore looked like unsafe plaintext even though the intended lifecycle is raw remote config -> managed SSH forward -> loopback websocket.
- Why this is root-cause fix: The fix changes the source-of-truth ownership boundary instead of suppressing the plaintext error downstream. Only callers that opt into owning the configured SSH tunnel may classify the raw config URL as pre-tunnel SSH transport, then they immediately start the tunnel, rewrite the runtime URL to `127.0.0.1:<localPort>`, and stop the owned tunnel when the call/client lifecycle ends or startup fails.
- Patch quality notes: Patch quality warnings for catch/default cleanup paths are intentional lifecycle guards: cleanup failures must not hide the original constructor, readiness, request, or already-closed startup result. The default/null returns model "no configured SSH owner" or test-only fixture behavior, not a silent fallback for failed requests. The larger diff is from adding regression coverage and applying the same ownership cleanup to one-shot calls plus bootstrap-based ACP, MCP, and operator-approval clients.
- Why it matters / User impact: Users following the documented safe remote Gateway setup can connect through managed SSH instead of being rejected before the tunnel exists, while unsafe direct plaintext remotes remain blocked.
- What did NOT change: This PR does not change CLI/env Gateway URL override safety, explicit `transport: "direct"`, status/health/doctor/TUI/security-audit/logs/devices/Crestodian probe behavior, WSS-over-SSH SNI behavior, reconnect restart behavior, schemas, or migrations.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: `src/gateway/connection-details.ts` remains the validation boundary for plaintext safety; `src/gateway/ssh-transport-config.ts` classifies configured SSH transport; `src/gateway/ssh-transport.ts` owns tunnel startup and runtime URL transformation; client owners are responsible for cleanup through call `finally` or `GatewayClient` shutdown.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan: This is an update to the existing same-contract PR #96134 for #26250, not a competing PR; the visible review findings are mapped in this body and the scope is kept to the existing PR's configured SSH Gateway transport contract.
- Out of scope: The latest local bot suggestion to extend configured SSH tunnel ownership into `buildGatewayProbeConnectionDetails` would expand this repair into health/doctor/status probe behavior, so it is intentionally not included in this issue-focused update.
- Target test file: Gateway transport/call/bootstrap/client/operator tests, infra SSH tunnel tests, ACP startup tests, and MCP channel bridge tests were run with the commands listed in the validation section.
- Scenario locked in: Config-derived SSH remotes may pass pre-tunnel validation only when an SSH target exists and the caller owns tunnel startup/cleanup; override/direct/missing-target paths still fail unsafe plaintext validation.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The regression tests lock the validation invariant, runtime URL rewrite, default SSH classification, remote port default, tunnel cleanup, and spawn-error behavior without changing unrelated probe surfaces.
- Risk labels considered: merge-risk availability, compatibility, security-boundary, auth-provider, message-delivery, and session-state signals were considered.
- Risk explanation: The security risk is accidentally widening plaintext allowance; the availability risk is leaking or failing to start SSH tunnels; the compatibility risk is honoring the documented omitted-transport SSH default for configs with `sshTarget`.
- Why acceptable: The allowance requires explicit tunnel ownership, config-derived URL source, SSH transport classification, and `sshTarget`, and the runtime target is loopback before websocket connection; focused tests and real OpenSSH/Gateway proof cover those boundaries.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #26250

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #26250

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No direct maintainer request; this follows the public issue report.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Configured SSH remote Gateway URLs are no longer rejected before the managed tunnel path can run; the tunnel rewrites the runtime URL to loopback; explicit `--url` plaintext overrides still fail the safety check.
- Real environment tested: Real OpenClaw CLI process, real foreground OpenClaw Gateway process, and an isolated local OpenSSH daemon using strict host-key checking, public-key auth, token auth, and `ssh -L` direct-tcpip forwarding. The configured remote URL used a non-loopback TEST-NET-3 host so the proof exercised the same plaintext guard boundary as the issue report without relying on an external server.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - Start an isolated OpenSSH daemon on loopback with generated host/client keys.
  - Start a foreground OpenClaw Gateway on a separate loopback port with token auth.
  - Configure the client profile with `gateway.mode: "remote"`, `gateway.remote.url: "ws://203.0.113.10:<localTunnelPort>"`, `gateway.remote.transport: "ssh"`, `gateway.remote.sshTarget`, `gateway.remote.sshIdentity`, `gateway.remote.remotePort`, and `gateway.remote.token`.
  - Run `openclaw gateway call health --json` through that config-derived SSH remote.
  - Run `openclaw gateway call health --url ws://203.0.113.10:<localTunnelPort> --token <token> --json` as the explicit override safety probe.
- Evidence after fix (copied terminal output):

  ```text
  Configured remote URL: ws://203.0.113.10:34829
  SSH target: 127.0.0.1:42069
  Remote Gateway port: 35601
  Local tunnel preferred port: 34829
  configured SSH gateway call exit: 0
  explicit --url override exit: 1
  sshd accepted publickey: True
  sshd observed direct-tcpip forwarding to Gateway: True
  leftover OpenClaw ssh forward process: none
  ```

  ```text
  Configured SSH health response:
  ok: true
  JSON keys included: agents, channelLabels, channelOrder, channels, defaultAgentId, durationMs, eventLoop, heartbeatSeconds, modelPricing, ok, plugins, sessions, ts
  ```

  ```text
  Explicit --url override safety probe:
  Gateway call failed: Error: SECURITY ERROR: Gateway URL "ws://203.0.113.10:34829" uses plaintext ws:// to a non-loopback address.
  Both credentials and chat data would be exposed to network interception.
  Source: cli --url
  Fix: Use wss:// for remote gateway URLs.
  ```

- Observed result after fix: The config-derived SSH remote opened an SSH session, sshd recorded public-key authentication and direct-tcpip forwarding to the real Gateway port, `openclaw gateway call health --json` returned `ok: true`, and the managed tunnel process was gone after the CLI call completed. The explicit `--url` override with the same plaintext non-loopback URL still failed the plaintext safety check.
- What was not tested: A public external SSH host was not used; the live proof used an isolated local OpenSSH daemon to avoid external credentials and network dependency while still exercising the real `ssh` binary, host-key checking, port forwarding, OpenClaw Gateway, and OpenClaw CLI.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The live proof validates the transport lifecycle and safety boundary without proving internet routing, remote host firewalls, or a production SSH account configuration.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/ssh-transport.test.ts src/gateway/client-bootstrap.test.ts src/gateway/call.test.ts src/gateway/client.test.ts src/gateway/operator-approvals-client.test.ts` — 12 test files, 549 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts` — 1 test file, 8 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/acp/server.startup.test.ts` — 1 test file, 15 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-src.config.ts src/mcp/channel-bridge.test.ts` — 1 test file, 20 tests passed, including the close-vs-bootstrap tunnel cleanup race.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Configured SSH transport opens a tunnel and rewrites the Gateway URL to loopback before client connection.
- Omitted `gateway.remote.transport` behaves as SSH when `sshTarget` is configured.
- Plaintext remote Gateway URLs are allowed only for callers that own the configured SSH tunnel.
- CLI/env URL overrides, explicit direct transport, and missing `sshTarget` still reject unsafe plaintext remotes.
- One-shot Gateway calls stop owned tunnels when auth validation or request execution fails.
- Bootstrap-based ACP, MCP channel bridge, and operator approval clients stop owned tunnels on shutdown, construction failure, readiness/startup failure, and close/bootstrap races.
- Omitted `gateway.remote.remotePort` forwards to remote Gateway port `18789`, while the configured URL port remains the preferred local listener.
- SSH spawn failures reject through `startSshPortForward` instead of becoming unhandled child-process errors.
- POSIX SSH tunnel startup uses `/usr/bin/ssh`; Windows keeps platform executable resolution.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- The issue reproduction path failed because the configured SSH remote URL was rejected by plaintext validation before tunnel setup.
- The default SSH transport regression test failed because `startSshPortForward` was not called when `remote.transport` was omitted.
- The MCP close-vs-bootstrap race regression failed when tunnel cleanup errors escaped an already-closed startup path.

If no test was added, why not?

Tests were added or updated for SSH transport classification, plaintext allowance scope, Gateway call/bootstrap paths, long-lived client cleanup, remote port defaulting, SSH launcher behavior, and SSH spawn failure handling.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Configured SSH remote Gateway users can now connect through the managed tunnel instead of being rejected before tunnel startup.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Existing documented SSH defaults are now honored in the managed SSH path; no migration is required.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. The network path changes for configured SSH remotes, but the plaintext allowance is scoped to config-derived SSH remotes with tunnel ownership, and the final runtime target is loopback.

What is the highest-risk area?

Accidentally widening plaintext `ws://` allowance beyond managed SSH ownership.

How is that risk mitigated?

The allowance requires all of: caller opt-in to owning the SSH tunnel, config-derived `gateway.remote.url`, SSH transport classification, and a configured `sshTarget`. CLI/env overrides, explicit direct transport, and missing `sshTarget` stay on the existing plaintext safety path. Focused tests cover each boundary.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

Ready for branch submission and CI.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

CI will rerun after branch submission. Local focused validation and live configured-SSH Gateway proof are complete. A full `pnpm check:test-types` run was also attempted and failed only in unrelated `extensions/qa-lab` type errors outside this PR's touched files.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

No maintainer review comments yet. Local RF mapping:

- RF-001: Disclosed as the current author-action label state; the branch update is intended to clear the waiting-on-author signal after CI/rereview.
- RF-002: WSS-over-SSH TLS hostname propagation is intentionally out of scope for this focused fix; this PR does not add SNI behavior.
- RF-003: Disclosed the SSH-default compatibility and plaintext-boundary risk in the summary and risk checklist for maintainer review.
- RF-004: Addressed by keeping omitted `gateway.remote.transport` on the documented SSH default only when an SSH target is configured, with regression coverage.
- RF-005: Addressed by limiting plaintext `ws://` allowance to config-derived managed SSH ownership with `sshTarget`; direct, CLI, and env override paths keep the guard.
- RF-006: WSS-over-SSH diagnostic probe TLS server-name propagation is intentionally out of scope after scope convergence.
- RF-007: The suggested TLS probe expansion was not taken because the PR is now focused on issue #26250's pre-tunnel rejection in owned Gateway call/bootstrap paths.
- RF-008: Security-audit probe changes are intentionally out of scope.
- RF-009: Doctor health probe changes are intentionally out of scope.
- RF-010: Crestodian probe changes are intentionally out of scope.
- RF-011: Security-audit WSS-over-SSH test command is intentionally out of scope because the security-audit path is not changed by this PR.
- RF-012: Doctor health WSS-over-SSH test command is intentionally out of scope because the doctor path is not changed by this PR.
- RF-013: Crestodian WSS-over-SSH test command is intentionally out of scope because the Crestodian path is not changed by this PR.

The local review findings addressed in code are the configured SSH default classification, the plaintext allowance boundary, managed tunnel startup before client connection, and tunnel cleanup on failure/shutdown paths.
